simple: Bindable events and bindable functions let scripts on the same side talk to each other, like two server scripts. A `BindableEvent` sends a one-way message, like 'the round started!', and any number of scripts can listen. A `BindableFunction` asks a question and waits for an answer, like 'what is 2 + 4?'. They are handy for round-based games, though ModuleScripts are often a better way to share data.
analogy: A BindableEvent is like a school announcement over the loudspeaker: everyone who is listening hears it, and the speaker does not wait for replies. A BindableFunction is like asking one friend a question and waiting for their answer.
keyPoints: Bindables only work between scripts on the same side: server to server, or client to client. For server-to-client, use remote events.
Put them in ServerScriptService for server scripts, or ReplicatedStorage for client scripts.
`BindableEvent:Fire(...)` sends a message without waiting. Listeners use `bindableEvent.Event:Connect(...)`.
Many functions can listen to one BindableEvent, but they run in no particular order. Combine them into one function if order matters.
`BindableFunction:Invoke(...)` waits for a reply. The other script sets `bindableFunction.OnInvoke = someFunction`, and its return value is sent back.
A BindableFunction has only one `OnInvoke` at a time; setting it again replaces the old one. If none is set, `Invoke` waits forever.
Tables you send are copied: non-string keys turn into strings, mixed number-and-name tables can lose items, and metatables are lost.

terms.BindableEvent: An object for sending a one-way message between scripts on the same side.
terms.BindableFunction: An object for asking another script on the same side to run a function and send back an answer.
terms.same side: Both scripts on the server, or both on the same player's device.
terms.asynchronous: Does not wait. The script that fires keeps running right away.
terms.synchronous: Waits for the answer before moving on.
terms.invoke: Call a BindableFunction (or RemoteFunction) and wait for its answer.
terms.callback: The function that runs when something is invoked, set with `OnInvoke`.
terms.yield: Pause and wait. `Invoke` yields until it gets the answer.
terms.thread: A separate line of work. Each listener runs in its own thread, so one error does not stop the others.
terms.metatable: A hidden table that adds extra behavior to another table. It does not survive being sent through a bindable.
terms.table identity: Which exact table something is. A sent table arrives as a copy, so it is not the same table, even if it has the same contents.

example.title: Announce when a round starts
example.place: BindableEvent named RoundStarted in ServerScriptService, plus two Scripts in ServerScriptService
example.code:
-- Script 1 (ServerScriptService): listens for the round to start
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local roundStarted = ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("RoundStarted")

roundStarted.Event:Connect(function(roundNumber)
	print("Starting timer for round " .. roundNumber)
end)

--[[ Script 2 (ServerScriptService, separate script): starts rounds
local ServerScriptService = game:GetService("ServerScriptService")
local roundStarted = ServerScriptService:WaitForChild("RoundStarted")

for round = 1, 3 do
	roundStarted:Fire(round) -- tell every listener
	task.wait(30) -- each round lasts 30 seconds
end
]]
explain: Both scripts find the same `BindableEvent` called RoundStarted.
Script 1 connects to `RoundStarted.Event` so it hears every announcement.
Script 2 calls `Fire(round)` to send the round number, then waits 30 seconds before the next round.
Each time Script 2 fires, Script 1 prints the round number. More scripts could listen too, like one to show a leaderboard.

watchOut: Bindables do not cross between the server and players. A server script firing a BindableEvent will not reach a LocalScript. Use a RemoteEvent for that.
If no script sets `OnInvoke`, calling `Invoke` freezes that script forever.
Do not send tables that mix numbered items and named keys. Send a pure list or a pure dictionary.
If the `OnInvoke` function has no `return`, the caller gets `nil`.
